summary: The pod named in the alert (checkout-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2kq9, container checkout-api) doesn't exist in this cluster. Instead, payments/checkout-api is fully down: its only pod, checkout-api-7f87c646c6-h6mj8 (container busybox), has restarted 12 times and has 0 of 1 replicas available. The container's hardcoded command prints "FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set" and runs `exit 1` every time, so it will crash even if DATABASE_URL is provided; the pod spec itself has to be fixed.
verified_facts: Pod payments/checkout-api-7d9f8c6b5-x2kq9 (from the alert) returns NotFound for both describe and logs.
The only pod matching app=checkout-api in payments is checkout-api-7f87c646c6-h6mj8: status Error, 0/1 ready, 12 restarts, age 36m, on node sre-agent-control-plane.
The pod's only container is named 'busybox' (not 'checkout-api' as in the alert), image busybox:1.36.
Container command is: sh -c 'echo FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set >&2; exit 1'. It has no Environment set and no envFrom/ConfigMap/Secret mounts besides the service account token.
Last state: Terminated, Reason Error, Exit Code 1. It starts and finishes in the same second.
Current container log output: 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set'. Previous container logs could not be retrieved ('unable to retrieve container logs').
Events show 37 BackOff warnings ('Back-off restarting failed container busybox') over 36m. The image pull worked, and there are no scheduling or OOM events.

Deployment checkout-api: created 19:55:44 +0530 (14:25:44Z) on 2026-10-27, annotation revision 1, OldReplicaSets <none>, 1 desired / 0 available, condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable).
The alert's startsAt (09:14:00Z) is earlier than this deployment's creation time (14:25:44Z).
The agent's service account can't read endpoints in payments (Forbidden), so service impact wasn't checked.
assumptions: The alert refers to this checkout-api deployment, even though its pod name, ReplicaSet hash, container name and start time don't match. It could be stale, for an earlier incarnation of the deployment, or from a different cluster.
checkout-api serves live checkout traffic, so 0 available replicas means customers are affected. SEV2 is based on this; downgrade if it's a non-prod or test workload.
The application is meant to read a DATABASE_URL from the environment (a Secret or ConfigMap). I didn't check whether such an object exists in payments.

hypotheses.cause: The deployment's pod template is broken. The container command is a placeholder that always prints a fatal error and exits 1, and no DATABASE_URL or app config is wired in, so the container can never start successfully.
evidence: The command is literally `echo FATAL: DATABASE_URL not set >&2; exit 1`, and the exit is unconditional.
Exit code 1 within the same second as start, on every one of the 12 restarts.
Environment: <none> in both the pod and the deployment template.
The image is a generic busybox:1.36, not a checkout-api application image.
The deployment is at revision 1 with no old ReplicaSets, so it may never have worked.
diagnostic_commands: kubectl get deployment checkout-api -n payments -o yaml

hypotheses.cause: The alert is stale or misrouted. It refers to an earlier deployment (ReplicaSet 7d9f8c6b5, container checkout-api) that was deleted and recreated as revision 1 with a different template, or it comes from another cluster's Prometheus.
evidence: The container name in the alert (checkout-api) differs from the actual container (busybox).
Alert startsAt 09:14Z is before deployment creation at 14:25:44Z.

hypotheses.cause: A required Secret or ConfigMap providing DATABASE_URL is missing or was deleted, and the real app image (not the busybox placeholder) fails for that reason.
evidence: The error text names DATABASE_URL specifically.
Weakened by: the running spec has no env references at all and hardcodes `exit 1`, so a missing secret isn't why this pod crashes.
diagnostic_commands: kubectl get deployment checkout-api -n payments -o yaml

safe_next_actions: Confirm who created or applied the payments/checkout-api deployment about 36 minutes ago (CI/CD or GitOps history) and whether the busybox placeholder spec was applied by mistake instead of the real manifest.
Check whether checkout traffic is affected: look at the Service, ingress and the upstream error rate. A human with endpoints read access should run `kubectl get endpoints checkout-api -n payments`.
Re-apply the correct checkout-api manifest from source control: the real image, a command that doesn't exit unconditionally, and DATABASE_URL coming from the right Secret.
Check that the DATABASE_URL Secret exists in payments before redeploying (`kubectl get secrets -n payments`).
Find out why the alert names a pod, container and start time that don't match the live object. Check the Alertmanager/Prometheus source cluster and whether kube-state-metrics series are stale.
rollback_plan: There's no in-cluster revision to roll back to: the deployment is at revision 1 and has no old ReplicaSets, so `kubectl rollout undo` won't help. Recovery means re-applying the last known-good checkout-api manifest from source control or GitOps, or reverting the commit or pipeline run that applied the busybox placeholder about 36 minutes ago.
